title: Primary Function
student: State the primary machining and structural function of the end mill.
instructor: The end mill removes material from the Aluminum 6061 workpiece while transmitting spindle torque and resisting cutting forces through its exposed shank into the holder and spindle.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Distinguish force components that generate bending and torsion.
student: Identify where cutting loads act. Which contribution bends the cutter, and which tangential contribution produces torque?
instructor: Cutting loads act near the engaged cutting edge. The transverse design force F bends the exposed cutter; the tangential component Ft acting at radius D/2 produces torque T = Ft(D/2).

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
student: Locate the cutter restraint and identify the appropriate simplified support condition at the tool holder.
instructor: The cutter is restrained at the holder face and idealized as fixed there. The exposed portion therefore acts as a cantilever.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace force and torque through the milling system.
student: Trace the force and torque path from the cutting zone through the end mill, holder, spindle, and machine structure.
instructor: Workpiece reactions act at the cutting edges, pass through the exposed cutter to the holder/collet, then into the spindle bearings and machine structure. Spindle torque follows the reverse path to the cutting zone.

title: Critical Location
learningObjectives: Locate the maximum moment and combined stress.
student: For the cantilever idealization, identify where the bending moment and nominal combined stress are largest.
instructor: The maximum bending moment occurs at the fixed holder face. There, bending normal stress and torsional shear stress are both maximum in magnitude at the outer surface.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
learningObjectives: Explain combined loading and identify excluded effects.
student: Explain why bending normal stress and torsional shear stress must be considered together. Identify important real effects omitted by the model.
instructor: Both components act at the same critical outer-surface point and form a combined stress state evaluated with von Mises stress. Omitted effects include flute-root stress concentrations, helical geometry, interrupted cutting, runout, chatter, fatigue, wear, temperature, and local cutting-edge failure.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify inputs controlling nominal static strength.
student: Identify the geometry, loading, and material variables needed for the strength assessment.
instructor: The calculation needs diameter D, overhang L, forces F and Ft, yield strength Sy, and required factor of safety nreq. Flute count, speed, depth of cut, and feed define the machining context.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Create a cantilever model before seeing the reference.
student: Draw the exposed end mill as a circular cantilever of diameter D and effective overhang L. Show transverse force F and torque T generated by Ft.
instructor: Show a fixed holder face, a solid circular cantilever of length L and diameter D, an end force F, and an axial torque T = Ft(D/2).

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State the assumptions defining the nominal model.
student: State the assumptions used to reduce the real fluted rotating cutter to a static Mechanics of Materials model.
instructor: Assume a prismatic solid circular shank, fixed holder face, static end loads replacing time-varying tooth contact, linear elasticity, and small deformation. Neglect flute-root stress concentrations, helical geometry, interrupted cutting, runout, chatter, fatigue, wear, thermal effects, and local cutting-edge failure.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
student: Outline the calculation sequence from applied loads to internal resultants, nominal stresses, equivalent stress, factor of safety, and assessment.
instructor: Compute Mmax and T; calculate I and J; calculate outer-surface bending and torsional stresses; combine them with von Mises; calculate factor of safety; compare with the requirement; and state limitations.

title: Boundary Condition and Internal Resultants
learningObjectives: Calculate the critical moment and torque.
instructor: The holder face is fixed. Mmax = ({{mill_F_N}} N)({{mill_L_mm}} mm) = {{mill_M_Nmm}} N·mm. T = ({{mill_Ft_N}} N)({{mill_D_mm}} mm/2) = {{mill_T_Nmm}} N·mm.

title: Bending Stress
student: Calculate σb = Mmax(D/2)/I at the critical outer surface near the fixed end.

title: Combined Stress
learningObjectives: Combine co-located normal and shear stresses.

title: Strength Factor of Safety
learningObjectives: Compare calculated and required factors of safety.
instructor: n = {{mill_Sy_MPa}} MPa/{{mill_sigma_vm_MPa}} MPa = {{mill_fos}}. The allowable equivalent stress is {{mill_sigma_allow_MPa}} MPa. {{mill_baseline_assessment}}

title: Strength Capacity and Sensitivity
learningObjectives: Solve for force at the required factor of safety.
student: Keeping Ft/F = 0.80 and all geometry fixed, determine F that would reduce the static factor of safety to exactly {{mill_n_req}}.

title: Engineering Assessment
student: State whether nominal static yielding governs for the baseline case. Explain at least two omitted real milling behaviors and why this factor of safety is not a complete tool-life prediction.
